initial_prompt: I need to process a difficult situation. My partner of 5 years just told me they don't love me anymore. I'm devastated. I don't know what to do.

messages.content: I need to process a difficult situation. My partner of 5 years just told me they don't love me anymore. I'm devastated. I don't know what to do.

I'm so sorry. Five years is a long time, and hearing those words - there's no way to prepare for that kind of blow. The devastation you're feeling makes complete sense.

I won't pretend to know exactly what you're going through, but I want to be here with you in this moment as best I can.

Can I ask - when did this happen? Are you in the immediate aftermath, or has it been a little while? And is there anything specific you're trying to figure out right now, or do you mostly need space to just... feel this?

Sometimes people want to process the "what now" questions. Sometimes they need to sit in the grief before any of that is possible. Sometimes they need to tell the story, to make it real by saying it. There's no right way.

What do you need right now?
It happened last night. I'm in shock I think. Part of me keeps expecting them to take it back. I don't even know how to be alone anymore. We were planning our whole lives together.

Last night. So you're right in the middle of it - that unreal space where the world has shifted but your mind hasn't caught up yet. The expecting them to take it back... that's not foolish, that's your whole nervous system trying to protect you from absorbing something this big all at once.

"I don't even know how to be alone anymore." I hear that. Five years of building a shared life, shared future, shared sense of who you are - and now that's been pulled out from under you. It's not just losing them, it's losing the version of yourself that existed in that "we."

You don't have to know how to be alone right now. You don't have to figure anything out today. Right now, you're in shock, and that's okay. That's your mind giving you time.

Is there someone who can be with you today - a friend, family member? Not to fix anything, just to be present? And are you somewhere safe, taking care of basics - have you eaten, slept at all?
